script:
Good morning, Shahriaar. Today is Monday, November 23. This is your morning brief.

Weather today is 10 degrees Celsius, partly cloudy. The high will be 19 and the low 10 degrees Celsius. Chance of precipitation is 13 percent.

You have 5 appointments in the next 24 hours: 8:30 AM, Meeting with Mr. Quds; 2:00 PM, Logistics; 3:00 PM, Design; 3:30 PM, Agency Sales Manager Interview; 4:30 PM, Guest.

Now, the top 5 stories in AI today.

First, from WIRED: Banks Have Had It Up to Here With Your AI Agent. Major US financial institutions are banning third-party AI agents from logging into customer accounts and warning that any costly mistakes made by bots are strictly the user's responsibility. The crackdown reflects rising enterprise resistance to autonomous AI systems accessing sensitive financial infrastructure. Why it matters: Directly affects AI agents and autonomous systems in enterprise settings, showing a major practical barrier to adoption in banking and finance.

Second, from The Verge: The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets. AI-assisted "vibe-coding" is expanding from software development into consumer gadgets and hardware devices. The trend indicates that natural language programming and AI coding tools are reaching physical products, potentially changing how people interact with and configure everyday technology. This represents a broader shift in AI coding and developer tools moving beyond traditional computers into new form factors. Why it matters: Relevant to coding and developer tools, showing AI-assisted programming expanding into hardware and consumer devices.

Third, from TechCrunch: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development. OpenAI's chief scientist is discussing how to establish a "speed limit" on AI development, arguing that the industry must first agree on how to measure AI progress before imposing constraints. The comments address AI governance and development pacing from one of the field's leading research organizations, offering insight into how frontier labs think about controlling the rate of AI advancement. Why it matters: Involves OpenAI, a major AI company, and addresses AI development governance and safety from its chief scientist.

Fourth, from TechCrunch: Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash. Data centers are at the center of growing Big Tech backlash as companies expand AI infrastructure, according to journalist Paris Marx's book "Hyperscale." The coverage examines tension between AI infrastructure buildout and public or regulatory resistance, highlighting challenges for firms expanding data center capacity to support AI workloads. This reflects broader scrutiny of the physical infrastructure underpinning AI expansion. Why it matters: Touches on AI infrastructure development, a key enabler of model training and deployment, though framed as industry backlash.

Fifth, from The Verge: We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages. Recent major tech outages include a nationwide FAA ground stop, a multi-day Outlook outage that disrupted businesses, and a JPMorgan Chase banking outage. Officials warn that more outages are likely. While not exclusively AI-focused, these infrastructure failures affect enterprise operations and highlight vulnerabilities in critical technology systems that businesses depend on daily. Why it matters: Affects enterprise operations broadly, but is not specifically an AI development, making it lower priority for an AI-focused briefing.

That is your brief. Have a great day.
